key_insight: ReMAP-PET teaches a 3D PET encoder to learn brain-region metabolic patterns, not just generic image features, by aligning PET with regional SUVR profiles.
clinical_relevance: This could improve PET-based neurodegenerative assessment by producing embeddings that are more interpretable, clinically meaningful, and usable for downstream diagnosis or reporting.
method: Partially tuned MedicalNet 3D ResNet-50 on paired PET and regional SUVR data
Optimized joint regression plus contrastive learning to match PET embeddings with metabolic profiles
Aligned metabolic embeddings with frozen BioClinicalBERT and generated PET-to-report text from SUVR constraints
evidence_signal: On 1,015 paired PET-SUVR samples, the model reached 0.070 SUVR MAE and 77.8% Recall@1, outperforming five frozen pretrained baselines.
watch_item: Results are promising but depend on paired regional SUVR supervision and may require careful validation across scanners, sites, and patient populations before broader use.
paper_title: ReMAP-PET: Beyond Visual Understanding -- Learning Region-Guided Metabolic Alignment Semantics from Brain PET
